Their versions are constrained by the\n# pyproject/lock at the pinned base commit above, so this layer is reproducible.\n#\n# Deliberately NOT here:\n#   * `pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel` — unpinned, so a later rebuild would\n#     silently build against a different resolver and build backend. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019ry67pRZetfLCAuSqtobtd","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t#!/usr/bin/env bash\n2\t# Behavioral verifier for Textualize__textual-5436-mm.\n3\t# Applies the synthetic test file (tests/test_key_panel_tooltip_alignment.py), runs the\n4\t# f2p + p2p tests and computes a reward from the JUnit XML report. NEVER greps source\n5\t# files for the fix — it runs the tests. No snapshot/SVG baseline is involved, so there\n6\t# is nothing an agent can regenerate.\n7\tset -uo pipefail\n8\t\n9\tmkdir -p /logs/verifier\n10\tSTDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt\n11\tSTDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt\n12\tREPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml\n13\t\n14\t: > \"$STDOUT_LOG\"\n15\t: > \"$STDERR_LOG\"\n16\t\n17\tensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }\n18\ttrap ensure_reward EXIT\n19\t\n20\tcd /app || { echo \"no /app\" | tee -a \"$STDERR_LOG\"; exit 1; }\n21\t\n22\t# ── Robustness + idempotency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n23\t# Restore EVERY path test.patch touches to the pristine harbor_base state BEFORE applying,\n24\t# so (a) agent edits to test files cannot affect scoring and (b) the apply stays idempotent\n25\t# on re-runs. Paths are read from `diff --git a/... b/...` headers, which are present for all\n26\t# entry types (text, binary, renamed, deleted) unlike `+++ b/`.\n27\t_patch_paths=$(\n28\t  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\\(.*\\) b/.*#\\1#p' /tests/test.patch\n29\t    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\\(.*\\)#\\1#p' /tests/test.patch\n30\t  } | sort -u\n31\t)\n32\tfor _p in $_patch_paths; do\n33\t  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- \"$_p\" 2>/dev/null \\\n34\t    || rm -f \"/app/$_p\" 2>/dev/null \\\n35\t    || true\n36\tdone\n37\tgit -C /app clean -fdq -- $(printf '%s\\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u) 2>/dev/null || true\n38\t\n39\techo \"== applying test.patch ==\" | tee -a \"$STDOUT_LOG\"\n40\tgit apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>\"$STDERR_LOG\" \\\n41\t  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>\"$STDERR_LOG\" \\\n42\t  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>\"$STDERR_LOG\" \\\n43\t  || { echo \"ERROR: could not apply test.patch\" | tee -a \"$STDERR_LOG\"; exit 1; }\n44\t\n45\t# ── Test-only deps ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n46\t# pytest + pytest-asyncio are test-only, so they are installed HERE at verify time rather\n47\t# than baked into the image, and at EXPLICIT PINS: an unpinned install would let a future\n48\t# pytest change collection behaviour and break a task that used to score correctly.\n49\t# These two pins are the versions this task's gate was reproduced against (oracle 1.0 /\n50\t# nop 0.0). Bump them deliberately, never implicitly.\n51\t#\n52\t# This is why task.toml sets `[verifier] network_mode = \"public\"` — the verifier phase needs\n53\t# egress to reach the index. It runs AFTER the agent phase is over and test.sh has restored\n54\t# the test files from harbor_base, so this egress cannot help a submission cheat; the AGENT\n55\t# phase stays sealed with `network_mode = \"no-network\"`.\n56\t#\n57\t# The synthetic test file imports only `rich`, `textual.app`, `textual.binding`,\n58\t# `textual.containers` and `textual.widgets`; BINARY -- there is no partial credit.\n\n    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes. A\n    strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is unsolved,\n    so it is 0.0.\n\n    reward is the same value, zeroed when the rubric judge failed a criterion. A \"pass\" or a\n    \"not graded\" verdict never lowers the score -- the judge must never be able to penalise a\n    run it could not grade.\n    \"\"\"\n    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)\n    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)\n    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q\n    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0\n    _canon.clear()\n    _canon.update({\n        \"reward\": 0.0 if rubric == \"fail\" else tests_passed,\n        \"tests_passed\": tests_passed,\n        \"f2p_passed\": f, \"f2p_total\": t,\n        \"p2p_passed\": p, \"p2p_total\": q,\n        \"rubric_passed\": {\"pass\": 1, \"fail\": 0}.get(rubric, -1),\n    })\n    return _canon[\"reward\"]\n\n\n@atexit.register\ndef _canon_flush():\n    if not _canon:\n        return\n    try:\n        _co.makedirs(_co.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)\n        with open(_CANON_JSON, \"w\") as _h:\n            _cj.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)\n        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and the\n        # lighthouse UI read reward.txt. Writing both from one dict means they cannot disagree.\n        with open(_CANON_TXT, \"w\") as _h:\n            _h.write(str(_canon[\"reward\"]))\n    except Exception as _exc:\n        print(\"WARNING: could not write %s: %s\" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=_cs.stderr)\n\n\ndef rubric_verdict(argv):\n    \"\"\"The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|\"\"`.\n\n    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh passes\n    when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means \"not graded\", which must never penalise the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if \"--rubric\" not in argv:\n        return None\n    i = argv.index(\"--rubric\")\n    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else \"\"\n    return value if value in (\"pass\", \"fail\") else None\n\n\ndef load_results():\n    \"\"\"Return {test_identifier: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} parsed from the JUnit report.\"\"\"\n    results = {}\n    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):\n        return results\n    tree = ET.parse(REPORT)\n    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):\n        classname = tc.get('classname', '')\n        name = tc.get('name', '')\n        # pytest junitxml classname is dotted module path; identifiers in config.json are\n        # \"path/to/file.py::test_name\" -- match tolerantly against both forms below.\n        full = f\"{classname}::{name}\".strip(':')\n        failed = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)\n        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)\n        results[full] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')\n    return results\n\n\ndef matched(idents, results):\n    \"\"\"Match each configured identifier against reported test names (substring tolerant,\n    since junitxml classnames use dotted module paths, e.g. tests.snapshot_tests.test_snapshots).\"\"\"\n    out = {}\n    for ident in idents:\n        test_name = ident.split('::')[-1]\n        hit = None\n        for k, v in results.items():\n            if ident in k or k.endswith(f\"::{test_name}\") or re.search(re.escape(test_name), k):\n                hit = v\n                break\n        out[ident] = hit or 'missing'\n    return out\n\n\ndef main():\n    results = load_results()\n    f2p = matched(F2P, results)\n    p2p = matched(P2P, results)\n    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p.items() if v == 'pass']\n    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p.items() if v == 'pass']\n\n    # Binary policy, applied by the canonical block: 1.0 only when every f2p passes and no\n    # p2p regressed. canon_reward writes reward.json and reward.txt via atexit, so it is the\n    # single writer and the two files cannot disagree.\n    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P),\n                          len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),\n                          rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))\n\n    # Per-test detail as extra FLAT SCALAR keys on the same dict (never a nested map, which\n    # harbor would reject). The aggregate counts cannot answer \"did THIS f2p test fail on nop?\",\n    # which is what proves no individual f2p test is inert.\n    for prefix, outcomes in (('f2p', f2p), ('p2p', p2p)):\n        for ident, outcome in outcomes.items():\n            _canon['%s::%s' % (prefix, ident.split('::')[-1])] = 1.0 if outcome == 'pass' else 0.0\n\n    print(json.dumps({'reward': reward, 'f2p': f2p, 'p2p': p2p}))\n\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n","numLines":155,"startLine":1,"totalLines":155}}}

b/tests/test_key_panel_tooltip_alignment.py\n@@ -0,0 +1,425 @@\n+\"\"\"The key panel must not pad a tooltip that has no description in front of it.\n+\n+`render_description` in the key panel joins a binding's *description* and its\n+*tooltip* with a single space.  When a binding carries **only** a tooltip there\n+is nothing to join it to, so the separator must not be emitted: otherwise every\n+description-less row is pushed one cell to the right of the description column\n+and the panel stops lining up.\n+\n+Two completely disjoint palettes are exercised:\n+\n+* an *archive browser* whose bindings live on the **App** and whose panel is\n+  raised through ``action_show_help_panel()`` (the ``HelpPanel`` route), at\n+  160x40; and\n+* a *query pane* whose bindings live on a focused **widget** and whose panel is\n+  a directly mounted ``KeyPanel``, at 120x26.\n+\n+They share no key, no size, no widget tree, no wording and no binding host, so a\n+fix keyed on any of those cannot satisfy both.  Every expectation is recomputed\n+at run time from the bindings the live application actually reports -- nothing\n+is transcribed from a screenshot or a stored baseline, and no snapshot is\n+involved.\n+\n+Both a state view (the Rich table the panel renders) and a behavioural view (the\n+text and segments the compositor actually paints) are asserted.\n+\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+from rich.table import Table\n+from rich.text import Text\n+\n+from textual.app import App, ComposeResult\n+from textual.binding import Binding\n+from textual.containers import Horizontal, Vertical\n+from textual.widgets import KeyPanel, Static\n+\n+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n+# helpers\n+# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n+\n+\n+def _bindings_table(app: App) -> Table:\n+    \"\"\"The Rich table the key panel renders for the current bindings.\"\"\"\n+    panel = app.query_one(KeyPanel)\n+    for node in panel.walk_children(with_self=True):\n+        renderer = getattr(node, \"render_bindings_table\", None)\n+        if renderer is not None:\n+            table = renderer()\n+            assert isinstance(table, Table), \"the key panel must render a Rich table\"\n+            return table\n+    raise AssertionError(\"the key panel does not contain a bindings table\")\n+\n+\n+def _cell_text(cell: object) -> Text:\n+    \"\"\"Normalise a Rich table cell to a `Text`.\"\"\"\n+    return cell if isinstance(cell, Text) else Text(str(cell))\n+\n+\n+def _description_cells(app: App) -> dict[str, Text]:\n+    \"\"\"Map every keyed row of the panel to its description cell.\n+\n+    Group-title rows (which have an empty key cell) are skipped.\n+    \"\"\"\n+    table = _bindings_table(app)\n+    assert len(table.columns) == 2, \"the bindings table has a key and a description column\"\n+    rows: dict[str, Text] = {}\n+    for key_cell, description_cell in zip(\n+        table.columns[0]._cells, table.columns[1]._cells\n+    ):\n+        key = _cell_text(key_cell).plain\n+        if not key:\n+            continue\n+        assert key not in rows, f\"duplicate key row {key!r}\"\n+        rows[key] = _cell_text(description_cell)\n+    return rows\n+\n+\n+def _title_cells(app: App) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"The plain text of every group-title row (rows with no key).\"\"\"\n+    table = _bindings_table(app)\n+    return [\n+        _cell_text(description_cell).plain\n+        for key_cell, description_cell in zip(\n+            table.columns[0]._cells, table.columns[1]._cells\n+        )\n+        if not _cell_text(key_cell).plain\n+    ]\n+\n+\n+def _own_bindings(app: App, action_prefix: str) -> list[Binding]:\n+    \"\"\"The non-system bindings this palette declares, as the app reports them.\"\"\"\n+    bindings = [\n+        active.binding\n+        for active in app.screen.active_bindings.values()\n+        if active.binding.action.startswith(action_prefix) and not active.binding.system\n+    ]\n+    assert bindings, f\"no active bindings for {action_prefix!r}\"\n+    return bindings\n+\n+\n+def _expected_descriptions(app: App, action_prefix: str) -> dict[str, str]:\n+    \"\"\"Recompute, from the live bindings, what each description cell part]\n+        expected[app.get_key_display(binding)] = \" \".join(parts)\n+    return expected\n+\n+\n+def _screen_lines(app: App) -> list[str]:\n+    \"\"\"Every line of composited screen output, {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BmBEbrXeqQZZALZDKMCKy2","type":"tool_result","content":"## `render_description` function\n\nThis nested function builds a `Text` object for a binding's description, appending tooltip text (dimmed) if present:\n\n```python\ndef render_description(binding: Binding) -> Text:\n    \"\"\"Render description text from a binding.\"\"\"\n    text = Text.from_markup(\n        binding.description, end=\"\", style=description_style\n    )\n    if binding.tooltip:\n        text.append(\" \")\n        text.append(binding.tooltip, \"dim\")\n    return text\n```\n\n## `DEFAULT_CSS` for `KeyPanel`\n\nThis CSS positions the panel on the right side of the screen and styles the nested `BindingsTable` components:\n\n```python\nDEFAULT_CSS = \"\"\"\nKeyPanel {                    \n    split: right;\n    width: 33%;\n    min-width: 30;              \n    max-width: 60;    \n    border-left: vkey $foreground 30%;\n    padding: 0 1;\n    height: 1fr;\n    padding-right: 1;\n    align: center top;\n\n    &> BindingsTable > .bindings-table--key {\n        color: $accent;           \n        text-style: bold;\n        padding: 0 1;\n    }\n\n    &> BindingsTable > .bindings-table--description {\n        color: $foreground;\n    }\n\n    &> BindingsTable > .bindings-table--divider {\n        color: transparent;\n    }\n\n    &> BindingsTable > .bindings-table--header {\n        text-style: dim italic;\n    }\n\n    #bindings-table {\n        width: auto;\n        height: auto;\n    }      \n}\n\"\"\"\n```\n\nIn short, the panel is docked to the right at roughly a third of the screen width (bounded between 30 and 60 cells), with distinct styling rules for key labels, descriptions, dividers, and section headers within the table it contains."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"f1bcf93e-c7b2-4430-9e73-49fe7f5370fb","uuid":"9852ab40-94aa-4fa4-a015-185bccd87b09","timestamp":"2026-08-13T22:58:45.495Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":5345,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"## `render_description` function\n\nThis nested function builds a `Text` object for a binding's description, appending tooltip text (dimmed) if present:\n\n```python\ndef render_description(binding: Binding) -> Text:\n    \"\"\"Render description text from a binding.\"\"\"\n    text = Text.from_markup(\n        binding.description, end=\"\", style=description_style\n    )\n    if binding.tooltip:\n        text.append(\" \")\n        text.append(binding.tooltip, \"dim\")\n    return text\n```\n\n## `DEFAULT_CSS` for `KeyPanel`\n\nThis CSS positions the panel on the right side of the screen and styles the nested `BindingsTable` components:\n\n```python\nDEFAULT_CSS = \"\"\"\nKeyPanel {                    \n    split: right;\n    width: 33%;\n    min-width: 30;
